morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with sex system, leaf width, and fruit: C. texensis is dioecious with separate male/female plants, narrow leaves, unisexual inflorescences, and a distinctly verrucose/warty capsule.
diagnostic_traits: annual herb with loose distal branching
styles more highly divided than the six-branch pattern of several local Crotons

confusers.separator: C. monanthogynus is monoecious, low and basal-branching with brown-dotted leaf undersides and a one-seeded capsule.
C. lindheimerianus is monoecious with bisexual racemes and smooth capsules rather than separate male/female plants.

morphology.look_here_first: Separate male and female plants, narrow leaves, unisexual inflorescences, and a distinctly verrucose/warty capsule.
morphology.key_separator: C. texensis is strictly dioecious; C. monanthogynus and C. lindheimerianus are monoecious. Its fruit is warty and styles are much more highly divided.
